title: Govern clarification dialogue and re-center drift

requirement.summary: Add a vendor-neutral advisory dialogue layer that keeps the user's business center visible, surfaces requirement or architecture drift, proactively asks one smallest useful question at a time, preserves normalized conclusions instead of raw conversation, and moves to a bounded human decision only when the options are actually stable.

objective.rationale: Single-select decisions reduce mechanical input only after the real choices are understood. Business, requirement, and architecture drift often require natural dialogue first. Treating every discussion turn as a gate or compressing material ambiguity into an early approval would optimize friction metrics at the expense of alignment.

goal: Define strict alignment-context, clarification-dialogue, clarification-prompt, and clarification-update contracts plus a multi-turn library/reference flow that preserves the center, classifies drift semantics, asks one question at a time, records only normalized human-owned summaries, and produces the existing minimal-input final decision only after clarification is ready.
non_goals: Do not make ordinary exploratory conversation create a development task, require admission, or count each turn as a governance decision episode.
Do not claim business value, product priority, requirement meaning, architecture correctness, or a recommended re-centering option is objectively determined by a static check.
Do not store raw prompts, raw answers, transcripts, assistant responses, source content, credentials, model identifiers, or absolute host paths in Core dialogue contracts.
Do not impose a product-level maximum number of clarification turns; bounded document size is an operational safety limit, not a semantic pressure to end discussion.
Do not let a Coding Agent mark a human answer, close an unknown, change the center, or select a final resolution without a trusted human-originated structured update or decision result.
Do not automatically admit or replace a task, change architecture policy, expand scope, approve an exception, start a session, execute commands, or authorize Git, deployment, publication, or release.
Do not add a hidden daemon, install a host component, add a second vendor Adapter, or claim cryptographic human identity.
acceptance_signals: A strict alignment-context contract separates the current center (outcome, why now, success, constraints, non-goals) from an advisory business, requirement, architecture, scope, or implementation drift observation, evidence, assumptions, unknowns, and denied authority.

A strict clarification-dialogue state keeps exact source identity and digest, revision, center, drift, open questions, normalized discussion records, candidate resolutions, alignment status, clarification-turn count, and governance-decision-episode count without raw conversation fields.

A proactive clarification prompt shows the current center, observed divergence, why the next question matters, and exactly one smallest useful natural-language question. Display and ordinary conversation grant no authority.

A strict human-originated clarification update binds the exact dialogue revision/digest and question, records a normalized answer summary plus explicit center/unknown/candidate changes, rejects unknown or raw fields, and cannot silently close or invent a different question.

Applying several valid updates advances immutable revisions without a product-level turn cap, counts clarification turns separately from governance decision episodes, and remains in dialogue until material unknowns are resolved and at least two bounded resolution options are stable.

Ready dialogue produces the existing digest-bound minimal-input human decision with return-to-center, adopt-new-center, split-new-requirement, continue-exploration, or stop options as applicable. The recommendation is advisory and never selected automatically.

A final human result can record only the selected alignment resolution and return a re-centered structured state; it does not itself mutate tasks, architecture documents, sessions, code, scope, Git, deployment, or release state.

Existing risk routing, decision prompts, exact ADMIT fallback, Coding Agent cards, JSONL, Codex Hooks, session, scope, completion, packaging, and repository behavior remains compatible; focused/full validation and governance checks pass.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_clarification_dialogue tests.test_human_decision tests.test_admission_routing tests.test_coding_agent_transport tests.test_agent_skills tests.test_task_contract -v

items: A Coding Agent could bias the stated center, drift framing, questions, or recommendations and present advisory interpretation as fact.
Premature readiness could turn unresolved ambiguity into a misleading quick approval.
Persisting raw discussion would create unnecessary privacy, portability, and context-retention risk.
Counting every conversational turn as an interruption could recreate bureaucracy and pressure users into bad early decisions.

stop_conditions: Stop if the implementation needs raw prompt, answer, transcript, response, source, credential, model, or absolute host-path retention.
Stop if an Agent-originated update can impersonate a human answer, resolve a material unknown, change the center, or record the final resolution.
Stop if a dialogue with unresolved material unknowns can become ready for final single-selection approval.
Stop if clarification turns are hard-limited for friction optics or counted as separate governance decision episodes.
Stop if an advisory drift is rendered as an objective failure or if final resolution directly changes task, architecture, session, code, scope, Git, deployment, publication, or release state.
Stop before any Git write, host installation, release, consumer mutation, deployment, or external-system write.

decision.rationale: The user reviewed the completed clarification core, accepted its center/drift and discussion-before-decision semantics, and explicitly continued to Adapter-driven automatic clarification on 2026-08-06.
